text:
alex: quick idea: add a "hydration_phases" contract to bundles for huge checkpoints (>1T). purpose: reduce peak OOM and make warmup deterministic.

maria: +1. how minimal can the manifest change be? we don't want every loader to become smart.

sam.b: main risk = tail latency when a request touches a cold phase. suggest pairing with a pinned lightweight fallback and a metric for fallback_rate.

kai: API-level primitive please: ensure_phase(name, strategy, timeout_ms). avoids ad-hoc loader heuristics.

lina: observability: per-phase latency histograms, hydration_fallback_rate, and trace spans named hydrate:phase:<name>. add alert if fallback_rate > 0.5% over 5m.

alex: manifest sketch (very small): phases: [ {name:meta}, {name:kvcache}, {name:layers-0-31}, {name:layers-32-63} ] + prefetch_hints. loader hydrates in order.

maria: streaming partial tokens from partially hydrated layers is risky; prefer short fallback response then retry.

sam.b: agree. fallback contract: bundle:compat:<level> pinned. also need percent_of_requests_fallback metric.

warmup-bot: perf-sim (bundle=gptx-1.5t-v2, policy=conservative) finished: median cold +22ms, 95p +320ms, mem peak -10%. link: https://ci.example/reports/3712345678

kai: migration note: add manifest_version and phase_uuid so older loaders detect boundary changes.

alex: i'll produce a test bundle and traces. sam.b, can you make a staging ticket to wire ensure_phase + fallback?
sam.b: yes, creating ticket now.
